prompt: To answer lowest-common-ancestor queries by range minimum, why record a node again whenever DFS returns from a child?

options.text: So the smallest node identifier becomes the answer.
options.explanation: Identifiers do not encode depth or ancestry.

options.text: So the interval between first visits includes the climb through their shared tree ancestor.
options.explanation: Correct. The minimum-depth node on that walk identifies the LCA.

options.text: So every node occurs exactly once.
options.explanation: Returning to a parent deliberately repeats it.

options.text: So the midpoint of every interval is its ancestor.
options.explanation: The query selects the shallowest node, not the midpoint.

workedExample: DFS records the walk down and back up. Between the first visits to two nodes, it climbs to their lowest common ancestor before reaching the other branch. The shallowest node in that recorded interval is the ancestor. Build an RMQ that retains the node identity or DFS-walk position along with depth; a numeric depth alone does not identify a node.
